name: Cable Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
summary: An isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi through shoulder extension using a high-pulley cable and rope attachment.

setup: Attach a rope attachment to the high pulley of a cable station.
Grasp each end of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing inward).
Take one to two steps back to create tension on the cable.
Hinge slightly forward at the hips with a flat back, soft knees, and arms extended forward overhead with a slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Brace your core and initiate the movement by sweeping your hands downward in a wide arc toward your thighs.
Maintain the fixed, slight bend in your elbows throughout the descent without turning the movement into a triceps pushdown.
Squeeze your lats firmly at the bottom as your hands reach the sides of your thighs, flaring the rope slightly apart for a deeper contraction.
Slowly raise your arms back along the same arc to the overhead position, feeling a full stretch in your lats before beginning the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the rope down toward your hips; inhale as you slowly return to the stretched starting position.
cues: Pull with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep the elbows frozen in a soft bend.
Chest tall and proud at the bottom squeeze.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows during the movement, turning it into a triceps extension.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend into your elbows from start to finish so that only the shoulder joint moves.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive body momentum or swinging the torso back and forth.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a stable hip hinge and braced torso throughout each rep, moving only the arms.

precautions: Ensure the cable attachment is fully secured to the carabiner before initiating load.
